findings.title: Apple speech-service agreement has no revocation control of its own; it is cleared only by withdrawing AI consent
findings.trigger: User allows Apple's speech service, later wants to revoke only that; or grants it while AI consent is not accepted (withdraw button is hidden in that state); or signs out / deletes the account.
findings.evidence: SOURCE INFERENCE. The only production call site of `revokeAppleServiceConsent()` is NucleoSession.swift:507 inside `revokeRiskNoticeConsent()` (grep over source/ found no other non-test caller). ios/Bobby/Sources/Nucleo/NucleoRootView.swift:141 passes `onWithdraw: session.profile.acceptedRiskNotice ? { ... } : nil`, so the withdraw action is absent when AI consent is not currently accepted. The key lives in UserDefaults (`speech.appleServiceConsent.v1`, NucleoSpeech.swift:89) and is not tied to the account. evidence/store-localizations/review-notes-en.txt:5 states "This consent is separate from the analysis AI permission"; granting is separate, revoking is not. Whether dictation is reachable before the risk notice is accepted was not verified. The iOS Settings speech-recognition switch remains a fallback.
findings.fix: Add a Profile row to revoke the Apple speech agreement independently, and clear the key on account deletion; or document that revocation is via AI-consent withdrawal or iOS Settings.

findings.title: Privacy policy describes the Apple-service gate differently from the app and the store listing
findings.trigger: Reading the policy next to the store description or review notes.
findings.evidence: PrivacyPage.tsx:201: "otherwise, and only after you have allowed speech recognition, the audio goes to Apple's speech service". The gate named is the iOS permission. The app requires an additional stored in-app agreement (NucleoSpeech.swift:183, 295; alert at NucleoSession.swift:457-463) and the store text says "only with your separate consent" (evidence/store-localizations/en-US/description.txt:18). PrivacyPage.tsx:202 says withdrawal "stops future AI analysis and generated-speech requests" and does not mention that it also removes the Apple speech agreement (NucleoSession.swift:507). The policy understates the protection; it does not overstate privacy. The page's tr() calls carry English and Spanish only in the lines read.
findings.fix: Add one sentence: Apple's speech service is used only after a separate in-app agreement, which is removed when AI consent is withdrawn.

findings.title: API TypeScript target omits api/bobby-access.ts, the Stripe checkout handler that iOS also calls; no TS2339 receipt in the snapshot
findings.trigger: `npm run check:api` (package.json:10 `tsc -p tsconfig.api.json`) passes while type errors exist in files outside the allowlist.
findings.evidence: tsconfig.api.json:21-117 is an explicit `include` allowlist with no `exclude`. It lists `api/stripe-webhook.ts` (line 111) and `api/account.ts` (line 73), so api/_lib/stripe-api.ts is reached through their imports (api/stripe-webhook.ts:13, api/account.ts:38). A grep of tsconfig.api.json for bobby-access, _lib/access, checkout-attempt, _lib/revenuecat, _lib/stripe-api returned 0 matches: api/bobby-access.ts (imports stripe-api at line 32, 40 Stripe references) is not a root and nothing imports an endpoint file. api/tsconfig.json:19 `"include": ["**/*.ts"]` would cover it, but no package.json script uses it (only lines 10 and 79 reference a tsconfig). The same endpoint serves iOS: ios/Bobby/Sources/BobbyAccess.swift:163 `static let accessPath = "api/bobby-access"`, and bobby-access.ts:293 handles Apple verification. The TS2339 errors are cited only in prose (brief.md:31, evidence/README.md:61); no tsc output exists in the snapshot, so their count and location are not verifiable. Impact on the iOS 1.7 (63) binary: none directly, as this is server code deployed separately; the risk is an unchecked server handler on the iOS access/levels/RevenueCat-sync path.
findings.fix: Add api/bobby-access.ts and its _lib dependencies to tsconfig.api.json (or run tsc with api/tsconfig.json in CI), capture the tsc output, and fix or annotate the TS2339 errors.

findings.title: Runtime UI evidence proves AI-consent withdrawal persistence, not the clearing of the Apple speech agreement
findings.trigger: Citing NucleoPrivacyUITests as end-to-end proof that withdrawal clears speech consent.
findings.evidence: PROVEN RUNTIME RESULT (Debug simulator, offline fixtures, English): evidence/NucleoPrivacyUITests-summary.json `passedTests: 2, failedTests: 0`; evidence/ui-serial-results.json:341-376. The test (lines 200-256) asserts the confirmation dialog, cancel without withdrawal, Profile and name preserved, and the risk gate returning after relaunch. It never reads `speech.appleServiceConsent.v1`, never exercises dictation, and does not assert that AI requests stop. Independent corroboration of persistence: evidence/native/StoreShots-consent-harness-remediation.json:16-18 `"agent.riskNoticeVersion": 0`. Speech-key clearing is covered only by mocked unit tests in source (ios/Bobby/Tests/NativeSpeechPipelineTests.swift:184-218, NucleoSpeechButtonTests.swift:143-144); I did not confirm those method names inside the 536-case test tree. No real SFSpeechRecognizer or physical-device run exists.
findings.fix: Add a UI or unit assertion that the defaults key is absent after `revokeRiskNoticeConsent()` through the Profile path, and run dictation once on a physical device with and without a local model.

findings.title: 1.6 on-device-only statement replaced by the consent-gated Apple-service fallback in code, usage string, risk notice and six store descriptions
findings.trigger: Hold-to-ask on a phone without a local model for the app language.
findings.evidence: SOURCE INFERENCE. NucleoSpeech.swift:294-298 `let onDevice = recognizer.supportsOnDeviceRecognition`, `guard onDevice || appleServiceConsent else { return .unavailable }`, request built with `onDevice: onDevice`; :261 `request.requiresOnDeviceRecognition = onDevice`; :148 consent read from UserDefaults on every call; :92 default prompt handler returns false; :213 stored only on Allow. ios/Bobby/Sources/Info.plist:56 and ios/Bobby/project.yml:116 name Apple's speech service; ios/Bobby/Sources/RiskNoticeView.swift:17 does too. Line 18 of each of the six evidence/store-localizations/<locale>/description.txt states the separate-consent fallback; a grep for 'never leaves / not uploaded / on-device only' equivalents across that directory returned no matches. Stale comment remains at nucleo/src/web/40-web-speech.js:4 ("Unlike iOS (R8, on-device only)"). de-DE and fr-FR line 18 use an imperative ("widerrufe deine Zustimmung im Profil", "retire ton autorisation") where English says "You can ... withdraw"; privacy meaning is unchanged.
findings.fix: Update the stale web comment; soften the de/fr imperative to 'you can'.
